subject: design-technology
title: Stretch: Cranks, Sliders and Ratchets
welcome_lead: Convert rotation into reciprocation and lock motion in one direction with ratchets and pawls.
meta_desc: Stretch into crank-and-slider, ratchet and pawl, and complex motion conversion.
final_note: You can recognise four basic motion types and convert between them with mechanisms.

concepts.def: Toothed wheel allowing motion one way only.
Spring-loaded lever that engages a ratchet.
Motion that spins around a point.
Swinging back and forth about a pivot.

walkthroughs.body_html: The four motion types are linear (straight), rotary (spinning), reciprocating (back and forth) and oscillating (swinging). Mechanisms exist to convert between them: pistons turn rotary into reciprocating, cams turn rotary into oscillating.
A crank and slider takes rotary input from a crank and gives reciprocating output along a slider. It is the heart of car engines (piston pushes crank) and sewing machines (crank pushes needle).
A socket wrench uses a ratchet and pawl so you tighten a bolt with one direction and the handle slips back without loosening it. The pawl drops into the next tooth ready for the next push.
